title: Uranium volumes in exported DRC cobalt >1% of global supply
gist: Benchmark's Uranium and Cobalt Services estimates uranium riding along in DRC copperbelt cobalt exports equals only 1-2% of Africa's total mined uranium supply, a negligible share of global supply, pushing back on alarm generated by a recent report on the topic.

themes.theme: Uranium in DRC cobalt: scale matters

insights.claim: Uranium contained in cobalt exported from the DRC's copperbelt region is estimated to be equivalent to only 1-2% of Africa's total mined uranium supply, making it a negligible portion of global uranium supply.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Quantifies and downplays concern about unrecorded uranium volumes in DRC cobalt exports as immaterial to global uranium supply or nuclear-security narratives.
insights.quote: The uranium contained in the DRC’s cobalt supplies is estimated to be equivalent to only 1–2% of Africa's total uranium mined supply, a negligible portion of global supply
insights.locator: The uranium contained in the DRC's cobalt supplies

insights.claim: Benchmark's analysis is explicitly framed as putting into context a recent report that highlighted the volumes of uranium contained in cobalt exports from the DRC, implying that report overstated the significance of those volumes.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Investors should discount headline-level alarm about contaminant or byproduct volumes in DRC cobalt exports without checking the claim against total global or regional supply base rates.
insights.quote: This puts into context a recent report highlighting the volumes contained in cobalt exports from the country.
insights.locator: This puts into context a recent report

insights.claim: Uranium occurs naturally as a trace element in DRC copperbelt cobalt and travels unrecorded through processing and export because the DRC has no formal testing infrastructure in place to track it.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Flags a traceability gap in DRC cobalt supply chains relevant to battery supply-chain due diligence, even though the absolute volumes involved appear small.
insights.quote: travels unrecorded through processing and export, as the country has no formal testing infrastructure in place

insights.claim: Unlike the DRC, other regions such as Australia deliberately recover uranium as a byproduct of copper mining rather than letting it pass through unrecorded, showing that formal byproduct-uranium recovery is an infrastructure choice some jurisdictions have made and the DRC has not.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Highlights a possible investable niche (byproduct uranium recovery infrastructure) or future regulatory flashpoint for DRC cobalt supply chains as traceability standards tighten.
insights.quote: Other regions, such as Australia, deliberately recover uranium as a byproduct of copper mining.
